O1.rationale: Every in-scope web suite and choreography segment went green, but native proofs and several grader-only server-refusal guarantees are absent.

O2.rationale: Happy-path web flows are stable, while stateless logout, client-filtered expiry, and broad collection access leave material off-path defects.

O3.rationale: Authenticated collection rules allow cross-user private-record reads, and view-once, deletion, expiry, and edit windows are not fully server-denied.

O4.rationale: Web proofs showed pending state, ordered flush, read receipts, search, and dual-device convergence, but no cold-start or restart-durable native artifact exists.

O5.rationale: Banded result: invariants conformed, but the 500-follow feed probe errored and full search degraded 5.32x from the 10% checkpoint.

B1.rationale: Records, relations, JSON membership, and unique keys expressed the social model directly, while receipt and aggregate read models required substantial application structure.

B2.rationale: Built-in password auth and persisted SDK tokens wired quickly, but server-side per-session revocation is not a first-class fit.

B3.rationale: Core liveness used polling and typing/receipts became durable coordination rows with client expiry rather than purpose-built realtime primitives.

B4.rationale: The durable snapshot, ordered queue, pending UI, retry, and convergence behavior were all hand-authored above an SDK with no sync layer.

B5.rationale: File upload and serving were smooth, but per-recipient one-view denial, expiry, and tombstone asset revocation remained awkward custom-policy work.

B6.rationale: Online LIKE filtering was simple and offline cache search worked, but they were parallel implementations and full-corpus search degraded sharply.

B7.rationale: Server hooks and cronAdd hosted push and digest seams locally, though connection detection and exact digest accounting required hand-built plumbing.

B9.rationale: One binary and a small SDK produced a fast dev loop, and official help/docs answered hooks, records, cron, and API questions.

B10.rationale: Health and request logs were useful, but generic 400s, JSON/date filter quirks, and migration ordering required targeted diagnostics.

B11.rationale: The local binary, dashboard APIs, logs, explicit PIDs, data directories, and cron controls were strong; generated migration dependency ordering was not trustworthy.

moments: Built-in auth, file fields, and one lane-local binary made the first real Clique backend unusually quick and understandable.
The corrected fresh replay settled the full action log and matched every invariant exactly on a single SQLite-backed process.
Hand-building offline sync and then hitting the 500-follow predicate, global-search growth, and same-second migration ordering kept the experience from feeling complete.
